Then He said: ﴿And Allah is ever Knowing and Wise﴾, meaning: He does not impose upon you anything, nor does He command you or forbid you except with what He knows to be a cause of your welfare in your religion and your worldly life.

[Page 27]

**Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 4, verses 105–106:**

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed, We have sent down to you the Book in truth, that you may judge between the people by that which God has shown you. And do not be an advocate for the treacherous.﴾ ﴿And seek forgiveness from God. Indeed, God is ever Forgiving and Merciful.﴾

Regarding the manner of the connection (al-nazm) there are several views:

The first: when God, exalted is He, had explained the circumstances of the hypocrites in detail, and then the matter of warfare followed, and with the mention of warfare came the legal rulings connected to it, such as the killing of a Muslim by mistake, supposing him to be an unbeliever, and such as the explanation of the prayer during travel and the prayer of fear, the discourse then returned to the circumstances of the hypocrites. He mentioned that they were trying to lead the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, to judge falsely and abandon the true judgment. So God informed His Messenger of this, and commanded him not to pay heed to them and not to accept their word in this matter.

The second view regarding the connection: when God, exalted is He, had explained the many rulings in this surah, He made clear that everything known is by the sending down of God, and that it is not permitted for the Messenger to deviate from any of them in pursuit of the pleasure of his people.

The third view: when God, exalted is He, commanded striving against the disbelievers, He made clear that although the matter is so, it is not permissible to act treacherously with them, nor to attribute to them what they did not do. And the disbelief of the disbeliever does not permit leniency toward him in judgment. Rather, what is obligatory in religion is that one judge for him and against him by what He sent down to His Messenger, and that no injustice befall the disbeliever in order to please the hypocrite. In the verse there are several issues:

The first issue: The exegetes agree that most of these verses were revealed concerning Tu'mah ibn Ubayriq. Then, regarding the details of the event, there are reports:

One of them: "Tu'mah stole a coat of mail. When the coat was demanded from him, he accused one of the Jews of that theft. When the dispute between his people and the Jew's people grew intense, his people came to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and asked him to assist them in this aim, and to attribute this betrayal to the Jew. The Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, then inclined toward this, and so the verse was revealed."

The second: a man deposited a coat of mail with him as a trust, and there was no witness. When he demanded it back, he denied it.

The third: when the depositor demanded the trust, he claimed that the Jew had stolen the coat.

Know that the scholars said: this indicates that Tu'mah and his people were hypocrites, for otherwise they would not have asked the Messenger to support falsehood and to attribute the theft to the Jew by way of baseless conjecture and calumny. And what confirms this is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿They do not mislead anyone but themselves, and they cannot harm you at all.﴾ [al-Nisa': 113]. Then it is related that Tu'mah fled to Mecca, apostatized, and broke into a wall there for the sake of theft, so the wall fell upon him and he died.

If it is asked: why did He say "habitual betrayer, sinful" (khawwanan atheeman), when what came from him was one betrayal and one sin?

We say: Allah, exalted is He, knew that this man's nature included much betrayal and much sin. So He mentioned the word that indicates emphasis, because of his inclination toward that. This is supported by what we have narrated: that after this incident he fled to Makkah and apostatized, and he broke into a man's wall for the purpose of theft, so the wall fell on him and he died. Whoever ends like that is not doubted to be a betrayer. Also, he asked the Prophet (ﷺ) to ward off the theft from him and attribute it to the Jew, and this nullifies the Messenger's mission. Whoever tries to nullify the Messenger's mission and seeks to show his lie has disbelieved. For this reason, Allah described him with emphasis in betrayal and sin.

It is also said: if you find a man committing an evil deed, know that it has siblings. It is reported from Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) that he ordered the hand of a thief to be cut off, and his mother came weeping and said: "This is his first theft, so pardon him." He said: "You have lied. Indeed, Allah does not take His servant to account at the very beginning of the matter."

Know that when Allah, exalted is He, restricted this threat to the one whose betrayal and sin are great, this indicates that whoever has little betrayal and sin is outside of it.

Then He, the Exalted, said: ﴿They hide themselves from the people, but they cannot hide themselves from Allah, for He is with them when they devise by night what He does not approve of in speech. And Allah is ever encompassing of what they do.﴾

Al-istikhfa' (concealment) linguistically means al-istitar (hiding oneself). One says: "istakhfaytu min fulan," meaning "I hid myself from him and concealed myself." He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And one who hides himself by night﴾ [Ar-Ra'd: 10], meaning, concealed. So His saying ﴿They hide themselves from the people﴾ means they conceal themselves from the people, and they do not conceal themselves from Allah.

Ibn 'Abbas said: "They are shy before the people and are not shy before Allah." Al-Wahidi said: "This is a meaning, not a tafsir (exegesis). That is because being shy before people necessitates concealing oneself from them and hiding from them. As for saying that al-istihya' (shyness) is the very same as al-istikhfa', the matter is not so."

His saying, ﴿and He is with them﴾, means with knowledge, power and sight. This is sufficient as a deterrent for a person from acts of disobedience.

His saying, ﴿when they devise by night what He does not approve of in speech﴾, means they harbour and plan in their minds. We have already explained the meaning of tabyit (nocturnal devising) in His saying: ﴿A faction of them spent the night devising other than what you say﴾ [An-Nisa': 81].

What Allah does not approve of in speech is that Tu'ma said: "I will accuse the Jew of being the one who stole the armour, and I will swear that I did not steal it, so the Messenger will accept my oath, because I am upon his religion, and he will not accept the oath of the Jew."

If it is asked: how is tabyit called speech when it is a meaning in the soul?

We say: Our position is that true speech is the meaning subsisting in the self (kalam al-nafs, inner speech). On this position there is no difficulty. Whoever denies inner speech may answer that Tu'ma and his companions probably gathered at night and arranged the manner of the scheme and deceit, so Allah, the Exalted, called their that discussion "the devised speech which He does not approve of."

As for His saying, ﴿And Allah is ever encompassing of what they do﴾, what is meant is a warning, from the standpoint that although they were concealing the manner of the deceit and fraud from the people, it was nonetheless manifest to the knowledge of Allah. This is because He, the Exalted, encompasses all things known, and nothing of them is hidden from Him, glorified is He.

Then Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿Here you are, you who argued on their behalf in the life of this world, but who will argue with Allah on their behalf on the Day of Resurrection?﴾ The particle (ha) in (ha antum) is for drawing attention (tanbih). (Ha antum) and (ha'ula'i) are a subject and predicate (mubtada' and khabar). The clause (jadaltum) is an explanatory clause (jumlah mubayyinah) for the occurrence of (ula'i) as a predicate, just as you say to one of the generous men: "You are Hatim, you give of your wealth and prefer others over yourself." It is also permissible that (ula'i) be a relative pronoun (ism mawsul) meaning "those who," and (jadaltum) be its relative clause (silah).

As for al-jidal (argument), linguistically it is an expression for intense contention (shiddat al-mukhasamah). Jadl al-habl means the intense twisting of a rope; a rajul majdul is one who seems to have been twisted; and al-ajdal is the falcon (al-saqr), because it is among the strongest of birds. This is the statement of al-Zajjaj. Others said: contention was named jidal because each of the two opponents wishes to turn his companion away from what he is upon and to divert him from his opinion.

Having understood this, we say: this is an address to a group of believers who used to defend Ta'mah and his people, because they outwardly appeared to be among the Muslims. The meaning is: Suppose you contended on behalf of Ta'mah and his people in this world, then who will contend on their behalf in the Hereafter when Allah seizes them with His punishment? And Abdullah ibn Mas'ud recited: "Ha antum ha'ula'i jadaltum 'anhu," meaning: on behalf of Ta'mah. His saying ﴿So who will argue with Allah on their behalf?﴾ is a question carrying the sense of rebuke and reproach.

Then Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿Or who will be a guardian (wakil) over them?﴾ His saying (am man yakunu) is conjoined (ʿatf) to the preceding interrogation. The wakil is the one to whom the affair is entrusted for protection and safeguarding. The meaning is: who is it that will be a protector and defender for them from the punishment of Allah?

Know that when Allah mentioned the threat in this context, He followed it with a call to repentance, and in it He mentioned three kinds of encouragement.

The first: Allah's saying: ﴿And whoever does evil or wrongs himself, then seeks forgiveness from Allah, will find Allah Forgiving and Merciful.﴾

By evil (su') is meant the ugly act that harms others, as Ta'mah did by stealing the armour and by accusing the Jew of theft. By wronging oneself (zulm al-nafs) is meant that which is confined to the person himself, such as a false oath. The reason that what extends to others is specifically named evil (su') is that it mostly results in conveying harm to others, and harm is present evil; whereas a sin that is confined to the person himself mostly does not amount to present harm, since a person does not convey harm to himself.

Know that this verse indicates two rulings:

The first: that repentance is accepted for all sins, whether they are disbelief or killing, deliberate or the seizure of wealth, because His saying ﴿whoever does evil or wrongs himself﴾ is general and encompasses all.

The second: that the apparent meaning of the verse requires that mere seeking of forgiveness suffices. Some said it is restricted to repentance, since seeking forgiveness does not benefit along with persistence. His saying ﴿will find Allah Forgiving and Merciful﴾ means: Forgiving and Merciful toward him; this qualification was omitted because the context indicates it, for there is no sense in encouraging seeking forgiveness unless that is what is meant.

The commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 4, verse 112:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And whoever earns a sin, he earns it only against himself. And Allah is ever Knowing and Wise.﴾

Al-kasb (earning, acquiring) is an expression for that which brings about the gaining of a benefit or the averting of a harm. For this reason it is not permissible to describe the Creator, exalted is He, with it. The purpose of the verse is to encourage the sinner to seek forgiveness (istighfar), as if He, exalted, were saying: "The sin you have committed does not return its harm to Me, for I am exempt from benefit and harm. Do not despair of the acceptance of repentance and seeking forgiveness." ﴿And Allah is ever Knowing﴾ of what is in his heart when he undertakes repentance, ﴿(Wise)﴾: His wisdom and mercy require that He pardon the one who repents.

The third type: His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And whoever earns a fault or a sin and then throws it onto an innocent person, he has certainly borne a slander and a manifest sin.﴾

The scholars have mentioned several views concerning khati'ah (fault) and ithm (sin):

The first: khati'ah is the minor sin, and ithm is the major sin.

The second: khati'ah is a sin confined to its doer, and ithm is a sin that extends to others, such as injustice and killing.

The third: khati'ah is that which should not be done, whether by intention or by mistake, and ithm is that which results from intention. The evidence for this is what precedes this verse, namely His saying: ﴿And whoever earns a sin, he earns it only against himself.﴾ So He clarified that ithm is that which is a cause for deserving punishment.

As for His saying ﴿then throws it onto an innocent person﴾, to what does the pronoun in "bihi" (with it) refer? There are several views:

The first: "then throws it with one of these two that have been mentioned."

The second: that it refers to ithm alone, since it is the nearest, just as it refers to trade in His saying: ﴿But when they see a trade or a diversion, they break away to it﴾ [al-Jumu'ah: 11].

The third: that it refers to kasb (earning), and the implied meaning is: "he throws his earning onto an innocent person," the verb yaksib indicating the kasb.

The fourth: that the pronoun refers to the meaning of khati'ah, as if He had said: "And whoever earns a wrong and then throws it onto an innocent person."

* * *

As for His saying ﴿he has certainly borne a slander﴾, al-buhtan (slander) is that you accuse your brother of a repugnant matter while he is innocent of it.

Know that the perpetrator of slander is blamed in this world in the most severe manner, and punished in the Hereafter with the most severe punishment. So His saying ﴿he has certainly borne a slander﴾ is an indication of the great blame that befalls him in this world, and His saying "and a manifest sin" is an indication of the great punishment that befalls him in the Hereafter.

Then God the Exalted said: ﴿And were it not for God's bounty upon you and His mercy, a group of them would have resolved to lead you astray﴾. The meaning: Were it not that God had singled you out with bounty, which is prophethood, and with mercy, which is protection (al-'ismah), a group of them would have resolved to lead you astray. This is because the people of Tu'mah had come to know that he was a thief, and then they asked the Prophet, peace be upon him, to defend him, argue on his behalf, clear him of the theft, and attribute that theft to the Jew. The meaning of "lead you astray" (yudilluka) is: cast you into a false and erroneous judgment.
* * *
Then God the Exalted said: ﴿And they do not lead astray except themselves﴾ through their cooperation in sin and transgression, and their giving false witness and slander. Since they undertook these deeds, they are the ones who act as the misguided do.
﴿And they cannot harm you at all﴾. Regarding this there are two interpretations:

The first: Al-Qaffal, may God have mercy on him, said: they cannot harm you in the future, so God promised him in this verse the continuation of protection for him from what they wish of casting him into falsehood.

The second: the meaning is that although they strive to cast you into falsehood, you did not fall into falsehood, because you built the matter upon the apparent state of affairs, and you were only commanded to build rulings upon outward appearances.

* * *
Then God the Exalted said: ﴿And God sent down to you the Book and wisdom﴾.
Know that if we interpret His saying ﴿and they cannot harm you at all﴾ to mean that God promised him protection in the future, then His saying ﴿and God sent down to you the Book and wisdom﴾ serves as a confirmation of that promise. That is, since He sent down to you the Book and wisdom and commanded you to convey the Sharia to creation, how would it be fitting for His wisdom not to protect you from falling into doubts and misguidance? And if we interpret that verse to mean that the Prophet, peace be upon him, was excused in building the ruling upon the apparent, the meaning would be: He sent down to you the Book and wisdom, and made obligatory within them the building of the rulings of the Sharia upon the apparent, so how would building the matter upon the apparent harm you?

* * *
Then God the Exalted said: ﴿And He taught you what you did not know, and the bounty of God upon you is ever great﴾.
Al-Qaffal, may God have mercy on him, said: this verse may bear two meanings:

One of them: that what is intended is what pertains to religion, as He said: ﴿You did not know what the Book is, nor faith﴾ [al-Shura: 52]. According to this meaning, the sense of the verse is: God sent down to you the Book and wisdom, and made you aware of their secrets, and acquainted you with their realities, although before that you knew nothing of them. Likewise He will act toward you in the coming days, so that none of the hypocrites will be able to mislead you or make you slip.

The second meaning: what is intended is: He taught you what you did not know of the reports of the earlier peoples, and likewise He teaches you the stratagems of the hypocrites and the forms of their plotting, by which you are able to guard against the forms of their deceit and scheming. Then He said: ﴿And the bounty of God upon you is ever great﴾. This is among the greatest proofs that knowledge is the most noble of virtues and merits, because God did not give creation of knowledge except a little, as He said: ﴿And you have been given of knowledge only a little﴾ [al-Isra: 85]. The share of a single person from the knowledge of all creation is small, yet He called that little "great" when He said: (﴿And you have been given of knowledge only a little﴾). And He called the whole of this world "little" when He said: ﴿Say, the enjoyment of this world is little﴾ [al-Nisa: 77]. This indicates the utmost nobility of knowledge.

Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 4, verse 114:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿There is no good in much of their secret talk, except for one who enjoins charity, or what is right, or reconciliation between people. And whoever does that seeking the pleasure of Allah, We will give him a great reward.﴾

Know that this is a reference to what they used to confer about when they plotted what He does not approve of in speech. There are several issues:

The first issue: al-Wahidi, may Allah have mercy on him, said: An-najwa (secret conversation) in the language is a secret between two people. It is said: "I conferred with the man" (nājaytu al-rajul munājāh and najā'), and it is said: "I conferred with the man" (najawtu al-rajul, anjū najwā), meaning: I conferred with him. An-najwa may be a verbal noun in the sense of al-munājāh (conferring), as He, the Exalted, says: ﴿There is no secret conversation of three but that He is their fourth﴾ [al-Mujadila: 7]. It may also mean the people who confer secretly, as He, the Exalted, says: ﴿when they are a secret conference﴾ [al-Isra': 47].

The second issue: His saying: ﴿except for one who enjoins charity﴾. The grammarians have mentioned several possibilities for the grammatical position of "man" (who), and these possibilities are based on the meaning of an-najwa in this verse. If we take the meaning of an-najwa here to be "secret," then it may be in the accusative position, because it is an exception of a thing from a category other than its own, so it is accusative, as in His saying: ﴿except harm﴾ [Al 'Imran: 111]. It may also be nominative, in the dialect of those who make the exception nominative when it is of a different category, as in the line of poetry:

"Except the sand-hills and except the she-camels"

Abu 'Ubayda considered this to be of the type of the elision of the mudaf (the governed noun), and said: The implied meaning is "except in the secret conversation of one who enjoins charity," then the mudaf was elided. On this reading, "man" occupies the position of an-najwa, since it has been placed in its stead, and there are two possibilities for it:
One of them: the genitive, as a substitute (badal) for "najwahum," as you say: "I did not pass by anyone except Zayd."

The second: the accusative, as an exception, as you say: "No one came to me except Zayd." This is an exception of a category from the same category.

As for if we take an-najwa to be the name of the people conferring, then it is accusative as an exception, because it is an exception of a category from the same category. "Man" may also be in the genitive position in two ways:

One of them: that you make it a follower of "kathir" (much), in the sense: there is no good in much of their secret talk except in the one who enjoins charity, as you say: "There is no good in the people except a few of them."

The second: that you make it a follower of an-najwa, as you say: "There is no good in a group of the people except Zayd." If you wish, you make Zayd a follower of the group, and if you wish, you make him a follower of the people. And Allah knows best.

The third issue: Although this verse was revealed concerning the secret talk of some of that thief's people with one another, its meaning is general. The intended meaning is: there is no good in what people confer about and engage in of speech, except what is of acts of goodness. Then He, the Exalted, mentioned three kinds of acts of goodness: enjoining charity, enjoining what is right, and reconciliation between people. Allah mentioned these three categories because a good deed is either by bringing benefit or by averting harm. As for bringing good, it is either of the bodily goods, which is giving wealth, and to this the reference is His saying: ﴿except one who enjoins charity﴾; or it is of the spiritual goods, which is an expression for perfecting the theoretical faculty with knowledge, or perfecting the practical faculty with good deeds, and the totality of these two is an expression for enjoining what is right, and to this the reference is His saying: ﴿or what is right﴾.

As for removing harm, to it refers

صفحة ٣٤
His saying: ﴿or reconciliation between people﴾. Thus it is established that the comprehensive forms of good are mentioned in this verse. And among what supports the correctness of what we have mentioned is his saying, upon him be prayers and peace: "All of the speech of the son of Adam is against him and not for him, except what is an enjoining of what is right, or forbidding of what is wrong, or remembrance of Allah."

It was said to Sufyan al-Thawri: How severe is this hadith! Sufyan said: Did you not hear Allah saying: ﴿There is no good in much of their secret talk﴾? It is this very thing. Did you not hear Allah saying: ﴿By time﴾ ﴿Indeed, mankind is in loss﴾ [al-'Asr: 1–2]? It is this very thing.

* * *
Then He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And whoever does that seeking the pleasure of Allah, We will give him a great reward.﴾ The meaning: these three categories of acts of obedience, although they are of the utmost nobility and majesty, a person benefits from them only if he performs them for the sake of Allah and seeking His pleasure. As for when he performs them for show and reputation, the matter is reversed, and they become among the greatest corruptions. This verse is among the strongest proofs that what is required of outward acts is attention to the states of the heart in sincerity of intention and purifying the motive from turning to any aim other than seeking the good pleasure of Allah, the Exalted. Its parallel is His saying: ﴿And they were not commanded except to worship Allah, sincere to Him in religion﴾ [al-Bayyina: 5], and His saying: ﴿And that there is not for man except what he strives for﴾ [al-Najm: 39], and his saying, upon him be prayers and peace: "Actions are only by intentions." Here there are two questions:
The first question: Why is "﴿seeking the pleasure of Allah﴾" in the accusative?

The answer: Because it is an object of purpose (maf'ul lahu), and the meaning is: because he seeks the pleasure of Allah.

The second question: How did He say: ﴿except one who enjoins﴾, then say: ﴿And whoever does that﴾?

The answer: He mentioned the enjoining of good so that it would indicate its doer, because since enjoining good has entered the company of the good-doers, it is more fitting that the doer of good should enter among them. It is also possible that what is meant is: "And whoever enjoins that," and he expressed the enjoining by the verb, because enjoining is also an act among the acts.

**Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 4, verses 115–116:**

The words of the Exalted: ﴿And whoever opposes the Messenger after guidance has become clear to him, and follows other than the way of the believers—We will leave him in what he has turned to and drive him into Hell, and evil it is as a destination.﴾

Know that the connection of this verse with what precedes it is what has been narrated: when Ta'mah ibn Ubayriq saw that Allah, the Exalted, had exposed him and cleared the Jew of the accusation of theft, he apostatized, went off to Makkah, and broke into a person's wall for the purpose of theft. The wall collapsed on him and he died, and this verse was revealed.

As for *shiqaq* (opposition) and *mushaqqah* (opposing), we have mentioned in Surat al-Baqarah that it is an expression for each of the two being on a different side of the matter, or for each of the two doing an act that entails hardship for the other. His words ﴿after guidance has become clear to him﴾ mean: after the truth of the religion of Islam has become evident to him through proof.

Al-Zajjaj (d. 311 AH) said: This Ta'mah had come to know, through what Allah, the Exalted, had revealed about his affair and what his theft had exposed, that this indicated the truth of the prophethood of Muhammad (ﷺ). So he opposed the Messenger, displayed opposition, and apostatized from the religion of Islam. Thus this was the manifestation of opposition after guidance had become clear to him. His words: ﴿and follows other than the way﴾

[Page 35]

(of the believers) mean: other than the religion of the monotheists. This is because Ta'mah abandoned the religion of Islam and followed the religion of idol worship.
* * *
Then He said: ﴿We will leave him in what he has turned to﴾, meaning: We will leave him and what he has chosen for himself, and entrust him to what he has taken as his guardian.

Some scholars said: This is abrogated by the verse of the sword, especially with regard to the apostate.

* * *
Then He said: ﴿and drive him into Hell﴾, meaning: We will oblige him to enter Hell. Its root is *al-sila'* (roasting at the fire), which is remaining by the fire at the time of seeking warmth. ﴿And evil it is as a destination﴾: the word (*masiran*) is in the accusative as a *tamyiz* (specification), like your saying: "So-and-so is good in soul" and "he sweated profusely (in sweat)." There are several issues concerning the verse:

**First issue:** It is narrated that al-Shafi'i, may Allah be pleased with him, was asked about a verse in the Book of Allah, the Exalted, that indicates that *ijma'* (scholarly consensus) is a proof. So he recited the Qur'an three hundred times until he found this verse. The structure of the argument is: following other than the way of the believers is forbidden, so following the way of the believers must be obligatory. The first premise is established as follows: He, the Exalted, attached the threat to the one who opposes the Messenger and follows other than the way of the believers. Opposing the Messenger alone necessitates this threat. If following other than the way of the believers did not necessitate it, then this would be adding to the threat something that has no effect on it, to something that by itself is sufficient to necessitate that threat; and that is impermissible. Thus it is established that following other than the way of the believers is forbidden. And once this is established, it follows that following the way of the believers is obligatory. This is because not following the way of the believers truly counts as following other than the way of the believers. So if following other than the way of the believers is forbidden, then not following the way of the believers is forbidden. And if not following them is forbidden, then following them is obligatory, because there is no exit from the two contradictory alternatives.

If it is said: We do not grant that not following the way of the believers truly counts as following other than the way of the believers, for it is not impossible that neither the way of the believers nor other than the way of the believers is followed.

This objection is answered as follows: *Muttabi'ah* (following) is an expression for doing the like of what another has done. So when it is the nature of non-believers not to follow the way of the believers, then whoever does not follow the way of the believers has done the like of the act of non-believers, and therefore he must be considered a follower of them. The objector may say: Following is not an expression for doing the like of another's act; otherwise it would have to be said that the prophets and angels are followers of individuals among creation insofar as they affirm the oneness of Allah, just as each individual of the community affirms the oneness of Allah. It is known that this is not said. Rather, following is an expression for doing the like of another's act *because* it is that other's act. And if that is so, then whoever abandons following the way of the believers, because he found no proof for the obligation of following them, does not follow them, and this person is not a follower of other than the way of the believers. This is a strong objection to this argument. There are other subtle discussions on it, which we have mentioned in the book *al-Mahsul fi 'Ilm al-Usul* (The Harvest in the Science of Principles). And Allah knows best.

**Second issue:** This verse indicates the obligation of the infallibility (*'ismah*) of Muhammad (ﷺ) from all sins. The proof for this is: if a sin were to proceed from him, it would be permissible to prevent him. And whoever prevents another from an act that the other performs is opposing him, because each of the two would be on a side other than the side the other is on. Thus it is established that if sin proceeded from the Messenger, opposing him would be obligatory. But opposing him is forbidden by this verse. Therefore sin must not proceed from him.

**Third issue:** This verse indicates that it is obligatory to emulate the Messenger, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him, in his actions. For if the action of the community were different from the action of the Messenger, it would follow that each of the two is on a different side of the work, and so opposition would occur. But opposition is forbidden. Therefore it is obligatory to emulate him in his actions.

[Page 36]

**Fourth issue:** Some of the earlier scholars said: Every *mujtahid* (qualified jurist exerting independent judgment) is correct in the fundamentals (*usul*), not in the sense that the belief of each of them corresponds to the reality, but in the sense that the sin is removed from the one who errs. They argued for their view with this verse, saying: Allah, the Exalted, made the occurrence of the threat conditional upon the clarity of guidance. Something conditioned on a condition is absent when the condition is absent. This implies that if the clarity of guidance does not occur, the threat does not occur.

Its answer: This is an argument from *mafhum* (implication of the opposite), which is a speculative (*zanni*) indication according to those who hold it. The proof showing that the threat against unbelievers is definitive is that after this verse He, the Exalted, said: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not forgive that partners be associated with Him﴾. And what is definitive is not opposed by what is merely probable.

**Fifth issue:** The verse indicates that the religion cannot be established except through proof, reflection, and reasoning. This is because He, the Exalted, made the occurrence of the threat conditional upon the clarity of guidance. And if the clarity of guidance were not a requirement for the validity of the religion, this condition would have no meaning.

**Sixth issue:** The verse indicates that *al-huda* (guidance) is a name for the proof, not for the knowledge. For if *al-huda* were a name for the knowledge, then "the clarity of guidance" would be the attribution of a thing to itself, and that is invalid.

Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 4, verse 117:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not forgive that He be associated with, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills. And whoever associates others with Allah has certainly strayed far astray.﴾ ﴿They invoke besides Him only females, and they invoke none but a rebellious Satan.﴾ ﴿Allah has cursed him, and he said: "I will surely take from among Your servants an appointed portion.﴾ ﴿And I will surely mislead them, and I will surely arouse in them false desires, and I will surely command them so they will slit the ears of cattle, and I will surely command them so they will alter the creation of Allah." And whoever takes Satan as a protector instead of Allah has certainly suffered a clear loss.﴾ ﴿He promises them and arouses desires in them, but Satan promises them nothing but delusion.﴾ ﴿Those, their refuge is Hell, and they will find no escape from it.﴾ ﴿But those who have believed and done righteous deeds - We will admit them to gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever. The promise of Allah is true, and who is more truthful than Allah in statement?﴾

Know that this verse is repeated in this surah, and in its repetition there are two benefits:

The first: the general statements of threat and the general statements of promise are in tension within the Qur'an. He, exalted is He, did not repeat any verse of threat with the same wording twice, yet He repeated this verse, which indicates pardon and forgiveness, with the same wording in one surah. Scholars agree that repetition has no purpose except emphasis. This indicates that He, exalted is He, gave the side of promise and mercy особое emphasis, and that this requires preferring promise over threat.

The second benefit: the preceding verses were revealed concerning the thief of the coat of mail, and His saying ﴿And whoever opposes the Messenger﴾ through the end of the verses was revealed concerning his apostasy. This verse fits well with what precedes it only if the meaning is that this thief, had he not apostatized, would not have become deprived of My mercy; but when he apostatized and associated others with Allah, he became definitively deprived of the mercy of Allah. Then He emphasized this by explaining that the matter of association is grave in the sight of Allah, so He said: ﴿And whoever associates others with Allah has certainly strayed far astray.﴾ That is, whoever does not associate others with Allah, his straying would not be far, and therefore he will not become deprived of My mercy. These connections certainly indicate the meaning of this verse: that everything other than association is definitely forgiven, whether repentance occurs or not. Then He, exalted is He, clarified that association is far astray, so He said: ﴿They invoke besides Him only females, and they invoke none but a rebellious Satan.﴾ ﴿Allah has cursed him.﴾ The word "in" (إنْ) here means negation, and its parallel is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And there is none of the People of the Scripture but that he will surely believe in it before his death.﴾ [An-Nisa: 159]. The word (يَدْعُونَ) [yad'una, "they invoke"] means (يَعْبُدُونَ) [ya'budun, "they worship"], because whoever worships something invokes it when he is in need of it. As for His saying ﴿only females﴾ (إلّا إناثًا), there are several views:

The first: the intended meaning is the idols, and they used to call them by names of females, as in their saying: al-Lat and al-Uzza and Manat, the third, the other. Al-Lat is the feminine form of Allah, and al-Uzza is the feminine form of al-Aziz. Al-Hasan said: No tribe of the Arabs existed but that it had an idol it worshipped and called "the female of the children of so-and-so." What confirms the soundness of this interpretation is the reading of 'A'isha, may Allah be pleased with her: (إلّا أوْثانًا) [illa awthanan, "only idols"], and the reading of Ibn 'Abbas: (إلّا أُثْنًا) [illa uthnan], the plural of (وَثَن) [wathan, idol], like (أسَد) [asad, lion] and (أُسْد) [usd, lions]; then the waw with a damma was changed into a hamza, as in His saying: ﴿And when the messengers are gathered at their appointed time﴾ [al-Mursalat: 11]. Az-Zajjaj said: It is possible that (أُثُنٌ) [uthunun] originally was (أُثْنٌ) [uthn], and the damma followed the damma.

The second view: His saying ﴿only females﴾ means only dead things (أمْواتًا) [amwatan, "dead/lifeless ones"]. Regarding calling the dead "females," there are two explanations:

The first: reporting about inanimate things is in the form of reporting about a female. You say: "These stones please me," just as you say: "This woman pleases me."

The second: the female is lower than the male, and the dead is lower than the living; for this reason of correspondence, they applied the name of the female to lifeless inanimate things.

The third view: some of them worshipped the angels, and they used to say: "The angels are the daughters of Allah." He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Indeed, those who do not believe in the Hereafter name the angels with the name of females﴾ [an-Najm: 27]. The purpose of the verse is: Is there any person more ignorant than one who associates with the Creator of the heavens and the earth and what is between them an inanimate thing that he names with a female name?

* * *

Then He said: ﴿And they invoke none but a rebellious Satan.﴾ The exegetes said: In each of those idols there was a satan who appeared to the custodians (al-sadana, "the keepers of the idols") and spoke to them. Az-Zajjaj said: The intended meaning of "Satan" here is Iblis, by the evidence that He, exalted is He, said after this verse: ﴿And he said: "I will surely take from among Your servants an appointed portion."﴾ There is no doubt that the speaker of this statement is Iblis, and it is not far-fetched that the one who appeared to the custodians was Iblis. As for "rebellious" (مَرِيدًا) [marid], it is one who is extreme in disobedience, complete in distance from obedience, and it is said of him: "marid" and "marid." Az-Zajjaj said: It is said: a "mumarrad" wall, meaning smooth; and it is said: a "marda" tree when its leaves have fallen; and the one who has not grown a beard is called "amrad" because the place of the beard is smooth. So whoever is extremely distant from obedience is called "marid" and "marid," because he is smoothed of obedience to Allah, and nothing of this obedience has adhered to him.

﴿Allah cursed him, and he said, "I will surely take from among Your servants an appointed portion."﴾ On this there are two issues.

The first issue: the author of *al-Kashshaf* said: His words ﴿Allah cursed him, and he said, "I will surely take..."﴾ are two descriptions, meaning a rebellious devil who combined the curse of Allah with this abominable statement. Know that the devil here has claimed several things.

The first of them is his saying ﴿I will surely take from among Your servants an appointed portion.﴾ In the language, *al-fard* means cutting. *Al-furdah* is the notch at the edge of a river. *Al-fard* is also the groove in a bowstring, and *al-fard* in a bow is the groove in which the string is fastened. *Al-fariḍah* is what Allah has made obligatory on His servants and made a firm obligation upon them, cutting off their excuse. Similarly is His saying ﴿and you have already specified for them a portion﴾ (al-Baqarah 2:237), meaning: you have assigned for them a portion of wealth.

Having understood this, we say: the meaning of the verse is that the devil, cursed by Allah, said at that time: "I will surely take from among Your servants a determined, specified share," namely those who follow his footsteps and accept his whisperings. In the *tafsir* (exegesis) it is related from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "From every thousand, one is for Allah, and the rest are for people and for Iblis."

If it is said: transmission and reason both indicate that the party of Satan is more numerous than the party of Allah.

As for transmission: Allah says concerning mankind: ﴿they turned away, except a few of them﴾ (al-Baqarah 2:246). And He reports from Satan: ﴿I will surely seize his descendants, except a few﴾ (al-Isra' 17:62). It is also related that he said: ﴿and I will surely mislead them all, except Your chosen servants among them﴾ (al-Hijr 15:39–40). There is no doubt that the chosen ones are few.

As for reason: the wicked and the disbelievers are more numerous than the sincere believers, and there is no doubt that the wicked and the disbelievers are all the party of Iblis.

Given this, we say: why did He say ﴿I will surely take from among Your servants a portion﴾ when the word *naṣīb* (portion) does not encompass the greater part but only the lesser?

The answer: this disparity arises only within the category of evil. But if you add the host of angels, together with their great multitude, to the believers, the dominance belongs to the sincere believers. Also, although the believers are few in number, their rank is great before Allah, while the disbelievers and the wicked, though numerous, are as nothing. For this reason the name *naṣīb* was applied to the people of Iblis.

The second of his claims: his saying ﴿and I will surely lead them astray﴾, meaning from the truth.

The Mu'tazilah said: This verse indicates two great principles of ours.

The first principle: the one who misguides is Satan, and it is not Allah the Exalted who misguides. They said: We said that the verse indicates that the one who misguides is Satan because Satan claimed that, and Allah the Exalted did not refute him in it. Its parallel is His saying: ﴿I will surely mislead them all﴾ [al-Hijr: 39], and His saying: ﴿I will surely seize his descendants, except for a few﴾ [al-Isra: 62], and His saying: ﴿I will surely sit in wait for them on Your straight path﴾ [al-A'raf: 16]. Also, He mentioned his description as one who misleads people in the context of blaming him, and that prevents the God from being described by that.

The second principle: Ahl al-Sunnah say that misguidance (al-idlal) is an expression for creating disbelief and error. We say: misguidance is not an expression for creating disbelief and error, as evidenced by the fact that Iblis described himself as one who misleads, even though by consensus he has no power to create error.

The answer: This is the speech of Iblis, so it is not a proof. Also, Iblis's speech on this matter is extremely confused. At times he inclines to pure predestination (qadar), and that is his saying: ﴿I will surely mislead them all﴾ [al-Hijr: 39]. At other times to pure compulsion (jabr), and that is his saying: ﴿My Lord, because You misled me﴾ [al-Hijr: 39]. And at times he shows hesitation in it when he said: ﴿Our Lord, these are the ones whom we misled; we misled them just as we ourselves were misled﴾ [al-Qasas: 63]. That is, the statement of these disbelievers: "We were misled, so who misled us from the religion?" And there must be an ending of all things in the Hereafter to Allah.

Third of them: His saying: ﴿and I will surely lead them astray﴾ [tumannihim]. Know that when he claimed that he misleads creation, he said: ﴿and I will surely lead them astray through false hopes﴾. This indicates that he has no stronger means of misguidance than casting false hopes (al-amani) into the hearts of creatures. Seeking false hopes produces two things: greed (al-hirs) and long hope (al-amal). Greed and long hope entail most blameworthy character traits, and they are like the two matters inseparable from the essence of man. The Prophet ﷺ said: "The son of Adam grows old, and two things grow young with him: greed and long hope." Greed entails undertaking the dangers of this world and the dangers of religion, for when a person's greed for something becomes intense, he may be unable to obtain it except by disobeying Allah and harming creatures. And when his hope is prolonged, he forgets the Hereafter and becomes immersed in this world, so he hardly ever proceeds to repentance, and admonition hardly affects him, and his heart becomes like stones or even harder in hardness.

Fourth of them: His saying: ﴿and I will surely order them, and they will surely slit the ears of cattle﴾. Al-batk means cutting, and a "sword batak" means a cutting sword, and al-tabtik means cutting into pieces. Al-Wahidi, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Al-tabtik here is the cutting of the ears of the baheerah by the consensus of the exegetes, for they used to slit the ears of a she-camel when she gave birth to five offspring and the fifth was a male, and they forbade themselves to benefit from her. Others said: The meaning is that they cut the ears of cattle as a rite (nusuk) in the worship of idols, so they think that this is worship, while in itself it is disbelief and transgression.

Fifth of them: His saying: ﴿and I will surely order them, and they will surely change the creation of Allah﴾. There are two opinions of the exegetes here:

The first: that what is meant by changing the creation of Allah is changing the religion of Allah. This is the view of Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, al-Hasan, al-Dahhak, Mujahid, al-Suddi, al-Nakha'i, and Qatadah. In establishing this view there are two aspects:

The first: that Allah the Exalted created creation upon Islam on the day He brought them out from the loins of Adam like atoms, and made them testify against themselves that He is their Lord, and they affirmed Him. So whoever disbelieves has changed the fitrah of Allah upon which He created people. This is the meaning of His ﷺ saying: "Every child is born upon the fitrah, but his parents make him a Jew, a Christian, or a Magian."

The second aspect in establishing this view: that what is meant by changing the religion of Allah is altering the lawful into the unlawful or the unlawful into the lawful.

The second opinion: to interpret this change as a change of states all of which relate to the outward, and they mentioned several aspects regarding it:

The first: al-Hasan said: What is meant is what Abdullah ibn Mas'ud narrated from the Prophet ﷺ: "Allah curses the women who join (al-wasilat) and the women who tattoo (al-washimat)." He said: That is because a woman reaches adultery through these acts.

The second: it was narrated from Anas, Shahr ibn Hawshab, Ikrimah, and Abu Salih that the meaning of changing the creation of Allah here is castration, cutting the ears, and gouging the eyes. That is why Anas used to dislike castrating sheep, and when the camels of one of the Arabs reached a thousand, they would blind the eye of its stallion.

The third: Ibn Zayd said it is effeminacy (al-takhannuth). And I say: on this view it is necessary to include female homosexuals (al-sahhaqat) in this verse, because takhannuth is an expression for a male resembling a female, and sahq is an expression for a female resembling a male.

The fourth: al-Zajjaj related from some of them that Allah the Exalted created the cattle so that they might ride them and eat them, but they forbade them to themselves, like the baheerah, the sa'ibah, and the wasilah. And He created the sun, moon, and stars subjugated to people, that they might benefit from them, but the polytheists worshipped them, so they changed the creation of Allah. This is the sum of what the exegetes said in this chapter. And there comes to my mind here another aspect in deriving the verse by way of meaning: that the entry of harm and disease into a thing occurs in three ways: disturbance (al-tashawwush), deficiency (al-nuqsan), and nullification (al-butlan). Satan, may Allah curse him, claimed to cast most of creation into the disease of religion, and the harm of religion is

His saying: ﴿and I will surely lead them astray﴾. Then this disease must be in one of the three aspects we mentioned: disturbance, deficiency, and nullification. As for disturbance, its indication is His saying: ﴿and I will surely lead them astray﴾; for the possessor of false hopes occupies his intellect and thought in extracting subtle meanings and fine stratagems and means in obtaining carnal and irascible desires, so this is a spiritual disease of the kind of disturbance. As for deficiency, its indication is His saying: ﴿and I will surely order them, and they will surely slit the ears of cattle﴾; for slitting the ears is a kind of deficiency. This is because when a person becomes absorbed in intellect in seeking the world, he becomes lukewarm in opinion and weak in resolve in seeking the Hereafter. As for nullification, its indication is His saying: ﴿and I will surely order them, and they will surely change the creation of Allah﴾; for change necessitates the nullification of the attribute present in the first period. It is known that whoever remains persistent in seeking immediate pleasures, turning away from spiritual felicities, his heart's desire for the world keeps increasing and his aversion from the Hereafter keeps growing, and these states continue to increase until the heart is completely changed, so that the remembrance of the Hereafter never occurs to his mind at all, and love of the world never leaves his thoughts at all, so his movement and stillness, his saying and doing, are all for the sake of the world. This necessitates a change of the created nature, for human souls entered this corporeal world as travelers, while they are oriented toward the world of resurrection. So when they forget their return and become accustomed to these sensible things which must come to an end and perish, this is in reality a change of the created nature, and it is as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And do not be like those who forgot Allah, so He made them forget themselves﴾ [al-Hashr: 19], and He said: ﴿Indeed, it is not the eyes that go blind, but it is the hearts within the breasts that go blind﴾ [al-Hajj: 46].

Know that when the Exalted related from Satan his claims regarding misguidance and error, He warned people against following him, saying: ﴿And whoever takes Satan as a guardian instead of Allah has certainly suffered a clear loss﴾. Know that no one chooses to take Satan as a guardian instead of Allah, but the meaning is that when he does what Satan commands him and leaves what the Most Merciful commands him, he is as if he has taken Satan as his own guardian and abandoned the guardianship of Allah the Exalted. And He said: ﴿has suffered a clear loss﴾ because obedience to Allah yields great, lasting benefits, pure of any admixture of harm, while obedience to Satan yields three benefits that are cut off and mixed with overwhelming sorrows, griefs, and pains, and combining the two is rationally impossible. So whoever desires his guardianship has lost the most noble and sublime of aims because of the basest and lowest of aims, and there is no doubt that this is absolute loss.

* * *

Then the Exalted said: ﴿He promises them and arouses desires in them, but Satan promises them nothing but delusion﴾. Know that we explained in the preceding verse that the main matter of Satan is only by casting false hopes into the heart; as for cutting the ears and changing the created nature, that is one of the results and effects of casting false hopes into the heart. Therefore Allah the Exalted surely drew attention to what is the main thing in repelling those false hopes, namely, that those false hopes produce nothing but delusion (ghurur). Delusion is that a person thinks of something that it is beneficial and delightful, then it becomes clear that it contains the greatest pains and harms, and all the states of this world are like that, and the intelligent person must not turn his attention to any of them. An example of this is that Satan casts into a person's heart that his life will be long, that he will attain from the world his hope and aim, that he will prevail over his enemies, and it occurs to his heart that worldly conditions are alternating, so perhaps it will be easy for him as it was easy for others. But all of that is delusion, for perhaps his life will not be long, and if it is long, perhaps he will not find his desired object, and if his life is long and he finds his desired object in the best manner, he will inevitably be at the moment of death in the greatest kinds of grief and regret; for the more delightful and desirable the object, and the more lasting and enduring the attachment to it, the more painful its separation, and the greater its effect in producing grief and regret. Thus it becomes clear that this verse alerts to what is the main principle and foundation in this matter.

Another aspect in the verse: that Satan promises them that there is no Resurrection and no recompense, so they strive to fulfill worldly pleasures.

* * *

Then the Exalted said: ﴿Those—their refuge is Hell﴾. Know that we have mentioned that delusion is the state that arises in a person upon finding something whose outward appearance is pleasing, but whose harm becomes greatly painful when the reality is revealed; and immersion in the delights of this world and indulgence in the disobedience of Allah the Glorified, though pleasant in the present, has as its end the punishment of Hell, the wrath of Allah, and distance from His mercy. So this meaning strengthens what was mentioned earlier, that it is nothing but delusion.

* * *

Then the Exalted said: ﴿And they will not find from it any escape﴾. Al-mahis means refuge and place of flight.

Al-Wahidi, may Allah have mercy on him, said: This verse may bear two meanings: First, that they must necessarily enter it. Second, the eternal abiding which is the portion of the disbelievers. This is not far-fetched, for the pronoun in His saying: ﴿and they will not find﴾ refers to those previously mentioned, who are those of whom Satan said: "I will surely take from Your servants an appointed portion." And the more evident view is that those who will be Satan's portion are the disbelievers.

When Allah mentioned the threat, He followed it with the promise, saying: ﴿And those who believed and did righteous deeds—We will admit them to gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever; the promise of Allah is true, and who is more truthful than Allah in statement?﴾

Know that the Exalted, in most verses of promise, mentioned: ﴿abiding therein forever﴾. If khulud indicated perpetuity and permanence, it would entail repetition, which is contrary to the principle; so we know that khulud is an expression for long duration, not for permanence. As for verses of threat, He mentions khulud and does not mention ta'bid except regarding the disbelievers, and that indicates that the punishment of sinners is finite.

* * *

Then He said: ﴿The promise of Allah is true (haqqan)﴾. The author of al-Kashshaf said: These are two infinitive nouns (masdar): First, it emphasizes itself, as if He said: "He promised a promise." And "haqqan" is an infinitive emphasizing something else, i.e., "that was true, truly."

* * *

Then He said: ﴿And who is more truthful than Allah in statement?﴾, and this is a third, emphatic, eloquent affirmation.

The purpose of these emphatic affirmations is to counter the false promises and vain wishes that Satan had conveyed to his followers, and to alert that God's promise is more deserving of acceptance and more worthy of belief than the words of Satan, than whom none is more lying.

Ḥamzah and al-Kisā'ī recited (أَصْدَقُ مِنَ اللَّهِ قِيلًا) with ishmām of the ṣād toward the zāy (ishmām: a partial, lip-rounded pronunciation mixing the sound with a zāy). The same applies to every unvowelled ṣād followed by a dāl in the Qur'an, such as (قَصْدُ السَّبِيلِ) [an-Naḥl: 9] and (فَاصْدَعْ بِمَا تُؤْمَرُ) [al-Ḥijr: 94].

Al-qīl is the verbal noun of qāla, qawlan and qīlan. Ibn al-Sikkīt said: al-qīl and al-qāl are two nouns, not two verbal nouns.

Therefore Allah the Exalted surely drew attention to what is the main thing in repelling those false hopes, namely, that those false hopes produce nothing but delusion (ghurur). Delusion is that a person thinks of something that it is beneficial and delightful, then it becomes clear that it contains the greatest pains and harms, and all the states of this world are like that, and the intelligent person must not turn his attention to any of them. An example of this is that Satan casts into a person's heart that his life will be long, that he will attain from the world his hope and aim, that he will prevail over his enemies, and it occurs to his heart that worldly conditions are alternating, so perhaps it will be easy for him as it was easy for others. But all of that is delusion, for perhaps his life will not be long, and if it is long, perhaps he will not find his desired object, and if his life is long and he finds his desired object in the best manner, he will inevitably be at the moment of death in the greatest kinds of grief and regret; for the more delightful and desirable the object, and the more lasting and enduring the attachment to it, the more painful its separation, and the greater its effect in producing grief and regret. Thus it becomes clear that this verse alerts to what is the main principle and foundation in this matter.

Another aspect in the verse: that Satan promises them that there is no Resurrection and no recompense, so they strive to fulfill worldly pleasures.

* * *

Then the Exalted said: ﴿Those—their refuge is Hell﴾. Know that we have mentioned that delusion is the state that arises in a person upon finding something whose outward appearance is pleasing, but whose harm becomes greatly painful when the reality is revealed; and immersion in the delights of this world and indulgence in the disobedience of Allah the Glorified, though pleasant in the present, has as its end the punishment of Hell, the wrath of Allah, and distance from His mercy. So this meaning strengthens what was mentioned earlier, that it is nothing but delusion.

* * *

Then the Exalted said: ﴿And they will not find from it any escape﴾. Al-mahis means refuge and place of flight.

Al-Wahidi, may Allah have mercy on him, said: This verse may bear two meanings: First, that they must necessarily enter it. Second, the eternal abiding which is the portion of the disbelievers. This is not far-fetched, for the pronoun in His saying: ﴿and they will not find﴾ refers to those previously mentioned, who are those of whom Satan said: "I will surely take from Your servants an appointed portion." And the more evident view is that those who will be Satan's portion are the disbelievers.

When Allah mentioned the threat, He followed it with the promise, saying: ﴿And those who believed and did righteous deeds—We will admit them to gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever; the promise of Allah is true, and who is more truthful than Allah in statement?﴾

Know that the Exalted, in most verses of promise, mentioned: ﴿abiding therein forever﴾. If khulud indicated perpetuity and permanence, it would entail repetition, which is contrary to the principle; so we know that khulud is an expression for long duration, not for permanence. As for verses of threat, He mentions khulud and does not mention ta'bid except regarding the disbelievers, and that indicates that the punishment of sinners is finite.

* * *

Then He said: ﴿The promise of Allah is true (haqqan)﴾. The author of al-Kashshaf said: These are two infinitive nouns (masdar): First, it emphasizes itself, as if He said: "He promised a promise." And "haqqan" is an infinitive emphasizing something else, i.e., "that was true, truly."

* * *

Then He said: ﴿And who is more truthful than Allah in statement?﴾, and this is a third, emphatic, eloquent affirmation.

The purpose of these emphatic affirmations is to counter the false promises and vain wishes that Satan had conveyed to his followers, and to alert that God's promise is more deserving of acceptance and more worthy of belief than the words of Satan, than whom none is more lying.

Ḥamzah and al-Kisā'ī recited (أَصْدَقُ مِنَ اللَّهِ قِيلًا) with ishmām of the ṣād toward the zāy (ishmām: a partial, lip-rounded pronunciation mixing the sound with a zāy). The same applies to every unvowelled ṣād followed by a dāl in the Qur'an, such as (قَصْدُ السَّبِيلِ) [an-Naḥl: 9] and (فَاصْدَعْ بِمَا تُؤْمَرُ) [al-Ḥijr: 94].

Al-qīl is the verbal noun of qāla, qawlan and qīlan. Ibn al-Sikkīt said: al-qīl and al-qāl are two nouns, not two verbal nouns.

ثُمَّ قالَ تَعالى: ﴿لَيْسَ بِأمانِيِّكم ولا أمانِيِّ أهْلِ الكِتابِ مَن يَعْمَلْ سُوءًا يُجْزَ بِهِ﴾ . وفِيهِ مَسائِلُ:

Then God, exalted is He, said: "It is not by your wishful thinking, nor by the wishful thinking of the People of the Book, that whoever does evil will be recompensed for it." On this verse there are several issues:

المَسْألَةُ الأُولى: الأُمْنِيَّةُ أُفْعُولَةٌ مِنَ المُنْيَةِ، وتَمامُ الكَلامِ في هَذا اللَّفْظِ مَذْكُورٌ في قَوْلِهِ تَعالى: ﴿إلّا إذا تَمَنّى ألْقى الشَّيْطانُ في أُمْنِيَّتِهِ﴾ [الحَجِّ: ٥٢] .

First issue: _umniyyah_ (wish, desire) is an _ufʿūlah_ form derived from _al-munyah_ (desire). The full discussion of this word is found in God's words: "Except when he [a prophet] wished, Satan threw [something] into his wish" (Q. 22:52).

المَسْألَةُ الثّانِيَةُ: لَيْسَ: فِعْلٌ، فَلا بُدَّ مِنَ اسْمٍ يَكُونُ هو مُسْنَدًا إلَيْهِ، وفِيهِ وُجُوهٌ:

Second issue: _laysa_ (is not) is a verb, so it must have a noun to which it is attributed as subject. On this there are several possibilities:

الأوَّلُ: لَيْسَ الثَّوابُ الَّذِي تَقَدَّمَ ذِكْرُهُ والوَعْدُ في قَوْلِهِ: ﴿سَنُدْخِلُهم جَنّاتٍ تَجْرِي﴾ الآيَةَ، بِأمانِيِّكم ولا أمانِيِّ أهْلِ الكِتابِ، أيْ

The first: "The reward and promise mentioned earlier, in God's words 'We shall admit them into gardens beneath which rivers flow' (Q. 4:122), is not [attained] by your wishful thinking nor by the wishful thinking of the People of the Book." That is:

صفحة ٤٢
لَيْسَ يُسْتَحَقُّ بِالأمانِيِّ إنَّما يُسْتَحَقُّ بِالإيمانِ والعَمَلِ الصّالِحِ.
الثّانِي: لَيْسَ وضْعُ الدِّينِ عَلى أمانِيِّكم.

it is not deserved through wishful thinking; it is deserved only through faith and righteous deeds.
The second: "The establishing of the religion is not based on your wishful thinking."

الثّالِثُ: لَيْسَ الثَّوابُ والعِقابُ بِأمانِيِّكم، والوَجْهُ الأوَّلُ أوْلى؛ لِأنَّ إسْنادَ ”لَيْسَ“ إلى ما هو مَذْكُورٌ فِيما قَبْلُ أوْلى مِن إسْنادِهِ إلى ما هو غَيْرُ مَذْكُورٍ.

The third: "Reward and punishment are not by your wishful thinking." The first possibility is preferable, because attributing _laysa_ to something already mentioned earlier is better than attributing it to something not mentioned.

المَسْألَةُ الثّالِثَةُ: الخِطابُ في قَوْلِهِ: ﴿لَيْسَ بِأمانِيِّكُمْ﴾ خِطابٌ مَعَ مَن ؟ فِيهِ قَوْلانِ:

Third issue: To whom is the address in "not by your wishful thinking" directed? On this there are two opinions:

الأوَّلُ: أنَّهُ خِطابٌ مَعَ عَبَدَةِ الأوْثانِ، وأمانِيُّهم: أنْ لا يَكُونَ هُناكَ حَشْرٌ، ولا نَشْرٌ، ولا ثَوابٌ، ولا عِقابٌ، وإنِ اعْتَرَفُوا بِهِ لَكِنَّهم يَصِفُونَ أصْنامَهم بِأنَّها شُفَعاؤُهم عِنْدَ اللَّهِ، وأمّا أمانِيُّ أهْلِ الكِتابِ فَهو قَوْلُهم: ﴿لَنْ يَدْخُلَ الجَنَّةَ إلّا مَن كانَ هُودًا أوْ نَصارى﴾ [البَقَرَةِ: ١١١] . وقَوْلُهم: ﴿نَحْنُ أبْناءُ اللَّهِ وأحِبّاؤُهُ﴾ [المائِدَةِ: ١٨] فَلا يُعَذِّبُنا، وقَوْلُهم: ﴿لَنْ تَمَسَّنا النّارُ إلّا أيّامًا مَعْدُودَةً﴾ [البَقَرَةِ: ٨٠] .

The first: It is addressed to idol-worshippers, whose wishful thinking is that there will be no gathering (of the dead), no resurrection, no reward and no punishment. Even if they acknowledged these, they describe their idols as their intercessors with God. As for the wishful thinking of the People of the Book, it is their saying: "None will enter the Garden except those who are Jews or Christians" (Q. 2:111); their saying: "We are the sons of God and His beloved" (Q. 5:18), so He will not punish us; and their saying: "The Fire will not touch us except for a number of days" (Q. 2:80).

القَوْلُ الثّانِي: أنَّهُ خِطابٌ مَعَ المُسْلِمِينَ، وأمانِيُّهم أنْ يَغْفِرَ لَهم وإنِ ارْتَكَبُوا الكَبائِرَ، ولَيْسَ الأمْرُ كَذَلِكَ، فَإنَّهُ تَعالى يَخُصُّ بِالعَفْوِ والرَّحْمَةِ مَن يَشاءُ، كَما قالَ: ﴿ويَغْفِرُ ما دُونَ ذَلِكَ لِمَن يَشاءُ﴾ [النِّساءِ: ١١٦] . ورُوِيَ أنَّهُ تَفاخَرَ المُسْلِمُونَ وأهْلُ الكِتابِ، فَقالَ أهْلُ الكِتابِ: نَبِيُّنا قَبْلَ نَبِيِّكم، وكِتابُنا قَبْلَ كِتابِكم، ونَحْنُ أوْلى بِاللَّهِ مِنكم، وقالَ المُسْلِمُونَ: نَبِيُّنا خاتَمُ النَّبِيِّينَ، وكِتابُنا ناسِخُ الكُتُبِ، فَأنْزَلَ اللَّهُ تَعالى هَذِهِ الآيَةَ.

The second: It is addressed to the Muslims, whose wishful thinking is that He will forgive them even if they commit major sins. But the matter is not so, for He specifies with pardon and mercy whomever He wills, as He said: "And He forgives what is less than that for whomever He wills" (Q. 4:116). It is reported that the Muslims and the People of the Book boasted to one another. The People of the Book said: "Our prophet came before your prophet, our book came before your book, and we are closer to God than you." The Muslims said: "Our prophet is the Seal of the Prophets, and our book abrogates the [previous] books." So God revealed this verse.

* * *
ثُمَّ قالَ تَعالى: ﴿مَن يَعْمَلْ سُوءًا يُجْزَ بِهِ﴾ وفِيهِ مَسائِلُ:
المَسْألَةُ الأُولى: قالَتِ المُعْتَزِلَةُ: هَذِهِ الآيَةُ دالَّةٌ عَلى أنَّهُ تَعالى لا يَعْفُو عَنْ شَيْءٍ مِنَ السَّيِّئاتِ، ولَيْسَ لِقائِلٍ أنْ يَقُولَ: هَذا يُشْكِلُ بِالصَّغائِرِ فَإنَّها مَغْفُورَةٌ قالُوا: الجَوابُ عَنْهُ مِن وجْهَيْنِ:

Then God, exalted is He, said: "Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it." On this there are several issues:
First issue: The Mu'tazilites said: This verse indicates that God does not pardon any of the bad deeds. Nor can anyone say: "This is problematic with regard to minor sins, since they are forgiven." They said: The answer to this is in two respects:

الأوَّلُ: أنَّ العامَّ بَعْدَ التَّخْصِيصِ حُجَّةٌ.

The first: A general (_ʿāmm_, universal) statement remains authoritative even after specification (_takhṣīṣ_).

والثّانِي: أنَّ صاحِبَ الصَّغِيرَةِ قَدِ انْحَبَطَ مِن ثَوابِ طاعَتِهِ بِمِقْدارِ عِقابِ تِلْكَ المَعْصِيَةِ، فَهَهُنا قَدْ وصَلَ جَزاءُ تِلْكَ المَعْصِيَةِ إلَيْهِ.

The second: The one who commits a minor sin has had his reward for obedience cancelled (_inḥibāṭ_) to the extent of the punishment for that disobedience, so here the recompense for that disobedience has reached him.

أجابَ أصْحابُنا عَنْهُ بِأنَّ الكَلامَ عَلى عُمُوماتِهِ قَدْ تَقَدَّمَ في تَفْسِيرِ قَوْلِهِ تَعالى: ﴿بَلى مَن كَسَبَ سَيِّئَةً وأحاطَتْ بِهِ خَطِيئَتُهُ فَأُولَئِكَ أصْحابُ النّارِ هم فِيها خالِدُونَ﴾ [البَقَرَةِ: ٨١] والَّذِي نَزِيدُهُ في هَذِهِ الآيَةِ وُجُوهٌ:

Our companions (the Ash'arites) answered that the discussion of its general terms has already passed in the commentary on God's words: "Yes, whoever earns an evil deed and is encompassed by his wrongdoing, those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein forever" (Q. 2:81). What we add regarding this verse are several points:

الأوَّلُ: لِمَ لا يَجُوزُ أنْ يَكُونَ المُرادُ مِن هَذا الجَزاءِ ما يَصِلُ إلى الإنْسانِ في الدُّنْيا مِنَ الغُمُومِ والهُمُومِ، والأحْزانِ والآلامِ والأسْقامِ ؟ والَّذِي يَدُلُّ عَلى صِحَّةِ ما ذَكَرْنا القُرْآنُ والخَبَرُ، أمّا القُرْآنُ فَهو قَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿والسّارِقُ والسّارِقَةُ فاقْطَعُوا أيْدِيَهُما جَزاءً بِما كَسَبا﴾ [المائِدَةِ: ٣٨] سَمّى ذَلِكَ القَطْعَ بِالجَزاءِ، وأمّا الخَبَرُ فَما «رُوِيَ أنَّهُ لَمّا نَزَلَتْ هَذِهِ الآيَةُ قالَ أبُو بَكْرٍ الصِّدِّيقُ -رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ-: كَيْفَ الصَّلاحُ بَعْدَ هَذِهِ الآيَةِ ؟ فَقالَ: غَفَرَ اللَّهُ لَكَ يا أبا بَكْرٍ ألَسْتَ تَمْرَضُ، ألَيْسَ يُصِيبُكَ الأذى ؟ فَهو ما تُجْزَوْنَ» .

The first: Why could it not be that the intended recompense is what reaches a person in this world of distress, sorrow, griefs, pains and illnesses? What confirms this is the Qur'an and a report. The Qur'an: God's words: "As for the male thief and the female thief, cut off their hands as a recompense for what they earned" (Q. 5:38), where He called that amputation a "recompense." The report: It is narrated that when this verse was revealed, Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (may God be pleased with him) said: "How can there be righteousness after this verse?" He (the Prophet) said: "May God forgive you, O Abu Bakr. Do you not fall ill? Does not harm befall you? That is what you are recompensed for."

«وعَنْ عائِشَةَ -رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْها- أنَّ رَجُلًا قَرَأ هَذِهِ الآيَةَ فَقالَ: أنُجْزى بِكُلِّ ما نَعْمَلُ ؟ ! لَقَدْ هَلَكْنا، فَبَلَغَ النَّبِيَّ ﷺ كَلامُهُ، فَقالَ: يُجْزى المُؤْمِنُ في الدُّنْيا بِمُصِيبَتِهِ في جَسَدِهِ وما يُؤْذِيهِ» . وعَنْ أبِي هُرَيْرَةَ -رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ-: «لَمّا نَزَلَتْ هَذِهِ الآيَةُ بَكَيْنا وحَزِنّا وقُلْنا: يا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ ما أبْقَتْ هَذِهِ الآيَةُ لَنا شَيْئًا، فَقالَ عَلَيْهِ الصَّلاةُ والسَّلامُ: ”أبْشِرُوا فَإنَّهُ لا يُصِيبُ أحَدٌ مِنكم مُصِيبَةٌ في الدُّنْيا إلّا جَعَلَها اللَّهُ لَهُ كَفّارَةً حَتّى الشَّوْكَةُ الَّتِي تَقَعُ في قَدَمِهِ“» .

It is related from ʿĀʾishah (may God be pleased with her) that a man recited this verse and said: "Are we to be recompensed for everything we do? We are destroyed!" His words reached the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "The believer is recompensed in this world by his affliction in his body and by whatever harms him." And from Abu Hurayrah (may God be pleased with him): "When this verse was revealed we wept and grieved and said: 'O Messenger of God, this verse has left us nothing!' The Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'Rejoice, for no one among you suffers a misfortune in this world except that God makes it an expiation for him, even the thorn that pricks his foot.'"

الوَجْهُ الثّانِي في الجَوابِ: هَبْ أنَّ ذَلِكَ الجَزاءَ إنَّما يَصِلُ إلَيْهِمْ يَوْمَ القِيامَةِ، لَكِنْ لِمَ لا يَجُوزُ أنْ يَحْصُلَ الجَزاءُ بِنَقْصِ ثَوابِ إيمانِهِ وسائِرِ طاعاتِهِ ؟ ويَدُلُّ عَلَيْهِ القُرْآنُ والخَبَرُ والمَعْقُولُ.

The second answer: Grant that this recompense reaches them on the Day of Resurrection. Why could it not be that the recompense occurs by reducing the reward of his faith and all his other acts of obedience? This is indicated by the Qur'an, a report, and reason.

أمّا القُرْآنُ فَقَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿إنَّ الحَسَناتِ يُذْهِبْنَ السَّيِّئاتِ﴾ .

The Qur'an: God's words: "Indeed, good deeds remove evil deeds" (Q. 11:114).

صفحة ٤٣
وأمّا الخَبَرُ: فَما رَوى الكَلْبِيُّ عَنْ أبِي صالِحٍ، عَنِ ابْنِ عَبّاسٍ أنَّهُ قالَ: «لَمّا نَزَلَتْ هَذِهِ الآيَةُ شَقَّتْ عَلى المُؤْمِنِينَ مَشَقَّةً شَدِيدَةً، وقالُوا: يا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ، وأيُّنا لَمْ يَعْمَلْ سُوءًا فَكَيْفَ الجَزاءُ ؟ فَقالَ عَلَيْهِ الصَّلاةُ والسَّلامُ: ”إنَّهُ تَعالى وعَدَ عَلى الطّاعَةِ عَشْرَ حَسَناتٍ وعَلى المَعْصِيَةِ الواحِدَةِ عُقُوبَةً واحِدَةً، فَمَن جُوزِيَ بِالسَّيِّئَةِ نَقَصَتْ واحِدَةٌ مِن عَشَرَةٍ، وبَقِيَتْ لَهُ تِسْعُ حَسَناتٍ فَوَيْلٌ لِمَن غَلَبَتْ آحادُهُ أعْشارَهُ“» .

The report: al-Kalbi related from Abu Salih, from Ibn ʿAbbas, that he said: "When this verse was revealed it weighed heavily upon the believers, and they said: 'O Messenger of God, which of us has not done evil? How then is the recompense?' The Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'He, exalted is He, promised ten good deeds for an act of obedience and one punishment for one act of disobedience. Whoever is recompensed for an evil deed loses one out of ten, and nine good deeds remain for him. Woe to him whose units outweigh his tens.'"

وأمّا المَعْقُولُ: فَهو أنَّ ثَوابَ الإيمانِ وجَمِيعَ الطّاعاتِ أعْظَمُ لا مَحالَةَ مِن عِقابِ الكَبِيرَةِ الواحِدَةِ، والعَدْلُ يَقْتَضِي أنْ يُحَطَّ مِنَ الأكْثَرِ مِثْلُ الأقَلِّ، فَيَبْقى حِينَئِذٍ مِنَ الأكْثَرِ شَيْءٌ زائِدٌ فَيَدْخُلُ الجَنَّةَ بِسَبَبِ تِلْكَ الزِّيادَةِ.

The rational argument: The reward of faith and of all acts of obedience is, without doubt, greater than the punishment for a single major sin. Justice requires that an equal amount be deducted from the greater, so that some surplus of the greater remains, and he enters Paradise by virtue of that surplus.

الوَجْهُ الثّالِثُ في الجَوابِ: أنَّ هَذِهِ الآيَةَ إنَّما نَزَلَتْ في الكُفّارِ، والَّذِي يَدُلُّ عَلى ما ذَكَرْناهُ أنَّهُ تَعالى قالَ بَعْدَ هَذِهِ الآيَةِ: ﴿ومَن يَعْمَلْ مِنَ الصّالِحاتِ مِن ذَكَرٍ أوْ أُنْثى وهو مُؤْمِنٌ فَأُولَئِكَ يَدْخُلُونَ الجَنَّةَ﴾ [النِّساءِ: ١٢٤] . فالمُؤْمِنُ الَّذِي أطاعَ اللَّهَ سَبْعِينَ سَنَةً ثُمَّ شَرِبَ قَطْرَةً مِنَ الخَمْرِ فَهو مُؤْمِنٌ قَدْ عَمِلَ الصّالِحاتِ، فَوَجَبَ القَطْعُ بِأنَّهُ يَدْخُلُ الجَنَّةَ بِحُكْمِ هَذِهِ الآيَةِ، وقَوْلُهم: خَرَجَ عَنْ كَوْنِهِ مُؤْمِنًا فَهو باطِلٌ لِلدَّلائِلِ الدّالَّةِ عَلى أنَّ صاحِبَ الكَبِيرَةِ مُؤْمِنٌ، مِثْلُ قَوْلِهِ: ﴿وإنْ طائِفَتانِ مِنَ المُؤْمِنِينَ اقْتَتَلُوا﴾ إلى قَوْلِهِ: ﴿فَإنْ بَغَتْ إحْداهُما عَلى الأُخْرى﴾ [الحُجُراتِ: ٩] سَمّى الباغِيَ حالَ كَوْنِهِ باغِيًا مُؤْمِنًا، وقالَ: ﴿ياأيُّها الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا كُتِبَ عَلَيْكُمُ القِصاصُ في القَتْلى﴾ [البَقَرَةِ: ١٨٧] سَمّى صاحِبَ القَتْلِ العَمْدِ العُدْوانِ مُؤْمِنًا، وقالَ: ﴿ياأيُّها الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا تُوبُوا إلى اللَّهِ﴾ [التَّحْرِيمِ: ٨] . سَمّاهُ مُؤْمِنًا حالَ ما أمَرَهُ بِالتَّوْبَةِ، فَثَبَتَ أنَّ صاحِبَ الكَبِيرَةِ مُؤْمِنٌ، وإذا كانَ مُؤْمِنًا كانَ قَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿ومَن يَعْمَلْ مِنَ الصّالِحاتِ﴾ حُجَّةً في أنَّ المُؤْمِنَ الَّذِي يَكُونُ صاحِبَ الكَبِيرَةِ مِن أهْلِ الجَنَّةِ، فَوَجَبَ أنْ يَكُونَ قَوْلُهُ: ﴿مَن يَعْمَلْ سُوءًا يُجْزَ بِهِ﴾ مَخْصُوصًا بِأهْلِ الكُفْرِ.

The third answer: This verse was revealed concerning unbelievers. What indicates this is that after this verse God said: "Whoever does righteous deeds, male or female, while being a believer, those will enter Paradise" (Q. 4:124). The believer who obeyed God for seventy years and then drank a drop of wine is still a believer who has done righteous deeds, so it is necessary to affirm with certainty that he enters Paradise by the ruling of this verse. Their claim that he has left the state of being a believer is false, because of the evidences showing that the perpetrator of a major sin is a believer, such as His words: "If two groups of believers fight, ... if one of them oppresses the other" (Q. 49:9). He called the oppressor, while oppressing, a believer. He also said: "O you who believe, retaliation is prescribed for you regarding the slain" (Q. 2:178), calling the perpetrator of deliberate, aggressive killing a believer. And He said: "O you who believe, turn to God in repentance" (Q. 66:8), calling him a believer at the very moment He commanded him to repent. Thus it is established that the perpetrator of a major sin is a believer. And since he is a believer, God's words "Whoever does righteous deeds" serve as proof that the believer who is a perpetrator of a major sin is among the people of Paradise. Therefore God's words "Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it" must be restricted to the people of disbelief.

الوَجْهُ الرّابِعُ في الجَوابِ: هَبْ أنَّ النَّصَّ يَعُمُّ المُؤْمِنَ والكافِرَ، ولَكِنَّ قَوْلَهُ: ﴿ويَغْفِرُ ما دُونَ ذَلِكَ لِمَن يَشاءُ﴾ [النِّساءِ: ٤٨] أخَصُّ مِنهُ، والخاصُّ مُقَدَّمٌ عَلى العامِّ؛ ولِأنَّ إلْحاقَ التَّأْوِيلِ بِعُمُوماتِ الوَعِيدِ أوْلى مِن إلْحاقِهِ بِعُمُوماتِ الوَعْدِ؛ لِأنَّ الوَفاءَ بِالوَعْدِ كَرَمٌ، وإهْمالَ الوَعِيدِ وحَمْلَهُ عَلى التَّأْوِيلِ بِالتَّعْرِيضِ جُودٌ وإحْسانٌ.

The fourth answer: Grant that the text is general, covering both believer and unbeliever. Yet His words "And He forgives what is less than that for whomever He wills" (Q. 4:48) are more specific, and the specific takes precedence over the general. Furthermore, applying interpretation to the general statements of threat is better than applying it to the general statements of promise, because fulfilling a promise is generosity, whereas neglecting a threat and interpreting it as an indirect warning is bounty and benevolence.

المَسْألَةُ الثّانِيَةُ: دَلَّتِ الآيَةُ عَلى أنَّ الكُفّارَ مُخاطَبُونَ بِفُرُوعِ الشَّرائِعِ؛ لِأنَّ قَوْلَهُ: ﴿مَن يَعْمَلْ سُوءًا﴾ يَتَناوَلُ جَمِيعَ المُحَرَّماتِ، فَدَخَلَ فِيهِ ما صَدَرَ عَنِ الكُفّارِ مِمّا هو مُحَرَّمٌ في دِينِ الإسْلامِ، ثُمَّ قَوْلُهُ: ﴿يُجْزَ بِهِ﴾ يَدُلُّ عَلى وُصُولِ جَزاءِ كُلِّ ذَلِكَ إلَيْهِمْ.

Second issue: The verse indicates that unbelievers are addressed with the branch rulings of the sharia, because "Whoever does evil" encompasses all prohibited acts, so it includes what the unbelievers do that is forbidden in the religion of Islam. Then His words "will be recompensed for it" indicate that the recompense for all of that reaches them.

فَإنْ قِيلَ: لِمَ لا يَجُوزُ أنْ يَكُونَ ذَلِكَ الجَزاءُ عِبارَةً عَمّا يَصِلُ إلَيْهِمْ مِنَ الهُمُومِ والغُمُومِ في الدُّنْيا ؟ .

If it is said: Why could that recompense not be the distress and grief that reach them in this world?

قُلْنا: إنَّهُ لا بُدَّ وأنْ يَصِلَ جَزاءُ أعْمالِهِمُ الحَسَنَةِ إلَيْهِمْ في الدُّنْيا إذْ لا سَبِيلَ إلى إيصالِ ذَلِكَ الجَزاءِ إلَيْهِمْ في الآخِرَةِ، وإذا كانَ كَذَلِكَ فَهَذا يَقْتَضِي أنْ يَكُونَ تَنَعُّمُهم في الدُّنْيا أكْثَرَ ولَذّاتُهم هَهُنا أكْمَلَ، ولِذَلِكَ قالَ عَلَيْهِ الصَّلاةُ والسَّلامُ: «”الدُّنْيا سِجْنُ المُؤْمِنِ وجَنَّةُ الكافِرِ“» وإذا كانَ كَذَلِكَ امْتَنَعَ أنْ يُقالَ: إنَّ جَزاءَ أفْعالِهِمُ المَحْظُورَةِ تَصِلُ إلَيْهِمْ في الدُّنْيا، فَوَجَبَ القَوْلُ بِوُصُولِ ذَلِكَ الجَزاءِ إلَيْهِمْ في الآخِرَةِ.

We reply: It is necessary that the recompense for their good deeds reach them in this world, since there is no way to deliver that recompense to them in the Hereafter. Given this, it follows that their enjoyment in this world is greater and their pleasures here more complete. That is why the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "The world is a prison for the believer and a paradise for the unbeliever." Since this is so, it is impossible to say that the recompense for their forbidden deeds reaches them in this world; therefore it must be affirmed that the recompense reaches them in the Hereafter.

المَسْألَةُ الثّالِثَةُ: قالَتِ المُعْتَزِلَةُ: دَلَّتِ الآيَةُ عَلى أنَّ العَبْدَ فاعِلٌ، ودَلَّتْ أيْضًا عَلى أنَّهُ بِعَمَلِ السُّوءِ يَسْتَحِقُّ الجَزاءَ، وإذا دَلَّتِ الآيَةُ عَلى مَجْمُوعِ هَذَيْنِ الأمْرَيْنِ، فَقَدْ دَلَّتْ عَلى أنَّ اللَّهَ غَيْرُ خالِقٍ لِأفْعالِ العِبادِ، وذَلِكَ مِن وجْهَيْنِ:

Third issue: The Mu'tazilites said: The verse indicates that the servant is the agent of his act, and it also indicates that by doing evil he deserves recompense. Since the verse indicates the combination of these two matters, it indicates that God is not the creator of the acts of His servants. This is in two respects:

أحَدُهُما: أنَّهُ لَمّا كانَ عَمَلًا لِلْعَبْدِ امْتَنَعَ كَوْنُهُ عَمَلًا لِلَّهِ تَعالى؛ لِاسْتِحالَةِ حُصُولِ مَقْدُورٍ واحِدٍ

The first: Since it is the servant's act, it cannot be God's act, because it is impossible for one single capability to be the object of two capable agents.

بِقادِرَيْنِ.
والثّانِي: أنَّهُ لَوْ حَصَلَ بِخَلْقِ اللَّهِ تَعالى لَما اسْتَحَقَّ العَبْدُ عَلَيْهِ جَزاءً البَتَّةَ وذَلِكَ باطِلٌ؛ لَأنَّ الآيَةَ دالَّةٌ عَلى أنَّ العَبْدَ يَسْتَحِقُّ الجَزاءَ عَلى عَمَلِهِ، واعْلَمْ أنَّ الكَلامَ عَلى هَذا النَّوْعِ مِنَ الِاسْتِدْلالِ مُكَرَّرٌ في هَذا الكِتابِ.
